raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46798. On SM90 it also needs the mHC change in #46523.

Identical greedy DeepSeek-V4.1 requests decode differently from run to run. The sparse top-k returns its selection in a different order each run, and on tied scores a different set, while sparse attention sums in index order. The issue shows this on SM120. We measured the same on H20 (SM90) and B300 (SM103); the per-path breakdown is in the issue comment.

#46522 makes top-k v2 keep the lowest positions among tied scores, and #46523 switches the SM90 mHC projection to `num_stages=1`. Together they make H20 deterministic in our tests. No open PR covers the remaining sources:
- Top-k v1 emits in thread-arrival order. This is the SM120 FullTopK path.
- `topk_transform_sparse` varies its order and, on bf16 ties, its set. It runs the SM100 candidate consumers in prefill and decode.
- DeepSelect's cluster tier varies its order and, on ties, its set. The tier is chosen by buffer width (`vocab_size > 16384`). The decode logits buffer is as wide as the page table (the maximum context length, not the current one), so SM100 FullTopK decode takes the cluster tier at every length.
- Top-k v2 still varies with more than 2048 exactly-equal scores, even with #46522.

This PR adds `SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK`, off by default. With it on, every DSV4 top-k entry point returns the same indices in the same order on every run.

## Modifications

- `srt/environ.py`: adds the flag.
- `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/topk.py`: with the flag on, `topk_transform_paged`, `topk_transform_paged_v2`, `topk_transform_ragged_v2` and `topk_transform_sparse` call `_deterministic_paged` / `_deterministic_ragged` instead of their kernels.
  - These use DeepSelect's single-CTA kernel when it accepts the operands. `_deep_select_takes` checks dtype, alignment, the 128-byte-padded last row, `k <= 4096`, and the page table.
  - Otherwise they use `_select_positions_torch`, an exact selection. It keeps every score above the k-th, then the lowest positions among the ties, and returns them in ascending order.
  - The page transform, output offsets and `-1` padding follow each entry point's contract. ROCm and XPU are unchanged.
- `kernels/ops/attention/deep_select.py`: with the flag on, buffers wider than the cluster threshold stay on the single-CTA kernel.
- `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/candidate_blocks.py`: `amax_topk_blocks` allocates its block keys with `aligned_new_empty`, giving 128-byte rows.
  - The default v2 path only needs `stride % 4`, so it is unaffected.
  - Without this change, keys for a 1M-token context (1048580 positions at ratio 1) do not end on a 128-byte boundary. With the flag on, DeepSelect then rejected them and the torch fallback cost about 0.2 ms per decode step on H20.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_deterministic_topk.py`: 99 new cases, described below.

## Accuracy Tests

The flag is off by default, so default outputs are unchanged. With it on, the selection is still an exact top-k. Among tied scores it may keep different positions than the default kernels, which pick ties arbitrarily.

**Kernel test** (H20): 99 passed in 14 s.
- Each entry point is run on rows with plateau ties and rows with bf16 ties, eager and under CUDA-graph replay, on DeepSelect and on the torch fallback.
- Each case checks run-to-run equality, top-k membership (as a score multiset), and the output contract.
- With the flag forced off, 38 of the 50 DeepSelect-side cases fail. The 12 that pass are inputs the default kernels already handle stably: trivial `seq <= k` rows, and rows whose top-k set has no ties.

**End to end.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8/EP8, radix cache off, temperature 0. The same prompt is sent 10 to 30 times per length, with and without a cache flush between runs, and logprobs are compared bit for bit.

| | main | this PR, flag on |
|---|---|---|
| H20, 3 nodes, nightly 586355a8, overlap scheduling on, 10 runs per length; both columns with #46523's mHC change | 511 identical; at 8193 / 9000 / 16385 / 33000 all 10 logprob vectors differ, on every node | identical at 511 / 8193 / 9000 / 16385 / 33000 on every node |
| B300, nightly a2cafa56, overlap scheduling on, 20 runs per length | 511: 7 to 8 different outputs in 20 runs; 8193 and 32769: all 20 logprob vectors differ | identical at 511 / 8193 / 32769 |
| B300, same image, overlap scheduling off, 30 runs per length | 511: 9 different outputs in 30 runs; 8193 and 32769: all 30 logprob vectors differ | identical at 511 / 8193 / 32769 |

Eight identical requests sent at once still differ by their position in the batch. That is batch invariance and out of scope here.

**GSM8K** (all 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, 128 in parallel), main vs flag on, on the overlap-on servers above. One standard error at this size is 0.008.
- H20, three nodes: 0.898 / 0.904 / 0.906 vs 0.904 / 0.902 / 0.900 (means 0.903 and 0.902)
- B300: 0.905 vs 0.911

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H20, TP8/EP8, three variants: main, flag off, flag on.

- **Decode GPU time per step**, 8K context, batch size 1, torch profiler over 40 steps: 10404 µs with the flag off, 10431 µs with it on (+0.26%). DeepSelect adds 66 µs and replacing top-k v2 saves 53 µs; kernels the flag does not touch, mostly the all-reduce, make up the rest.
- **bench_serving** (random ids), main / flag off / flag on:
  - TPOT, 8K, batch size 1: 8.10 / 8.10 / 8.11 ms
  - TPOT, 32K, batch size 1: 8.15 / 8.14 / 8.19 ms
  - TPOT, 8K, concurrency 16: 13.81 / 13.86 / 14.23 ms (single run)
  - TTFT: all within ±2%
- **bench_serving rerun** on two nodes, main vs flag on, both with #46523's mHC change:
  - TPOT, 8K, batch size 1: 8.09 → 8.11 and 8.10 → 8.11 ms
  - TPOT, 32K, batch size 1: 8.15 → 8.19 and 8.16 → 8.20 ms
  - TPOT, 8K, concurrency 16: 13.43 → 13.59 and 13.83 → 13.64 ms. Main alone ranges from 13.43 to 13.83 ms across the three runs, so the +3% of the single run above is within run-to-run spread.
  - TTFT, 2K to 32K: within ±1.7%. Output throughput of the decode configs: within ±0.2%.
  - A third node is slower across the board (TPOT at concurrency 16: 24.8 ms), so its numbers are not listed. Its flag-on deltas are within ±1.2% for TPOT and ±3% for TTFT.
- **Per call under CUDA graph**, flag off vs on:
  - Top-k v2 paged fp32, 8193 positions: 5.5 → 10.1 µs
  - DeepSelect bf16, 65536 positions (single-CTA instead of the cluster tier): 6.8 → 12.3 µs

B300, TP8/EP8, default arguments, overlap scheduling on, main vs flag on, bench_serving (random ids), single run:
- TPOT, 8K, batch size 1: 4.80 → 4.84 ms
- TPOT, 32K, batch size 1: 4.86 → 4.81 ms
- TPOT, 8K, concurrency 16: 6.11 → 6.11 ms
- TTFT, prefill only, 2K / 8K / 32K: 154.5 → 153.5, 164.9 → 161.1, 551.9 → 548.7 ms
- TTFT of the same three decode runs: 169.5 → 177.2, 552.1 → 557.7, 1303 → 1335 ms (+4.5%, +1.0%, +2.5%)

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide. Ran ruff, ruff-format, isort and codespell, plus `check-registered-tests` and `check-no-bare-pytest-main`.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests guide.
- [ ] Update documentation according to the Write documentations guide. Only the `environ.py` comment documents the flag.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the Test the accuracy and Benchmark the speed guides.

     make_cpp_args,
 )
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.deep_select import get_input_stride_alignment_bytes
 
 from .candidate_table import CANDIDATE_BLOCK_SIZE
 from .topk import plan_topk_v2, topk_transform_paged_v2
@@ -137,9 +139,13 @@ def amax_topk_blocks(
     # NOTE: plan cannot be the previous kernel of topk_transform_paged_v2
     plan = plan_topk_v2(nblocks)
     # block maxima, the newest block +inf; the top-k reads each row up to nblocks
-    # only, so nothing past a row's keys is initialised (v2 needs stride % 4 == 0)
-    keys = logits.new_empty(

+    # only, so nothing past a row's keys is initialised (v2 needs stride % 4 == 0,
+    # DeepSelect under SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK rows of 128 bytes)
+    keys = aligned_new_empty(
+        (rows, -(-max_seq_len // (4 * block)) * 4),
+        torch.float32,
+        logits.device,
+        alignment_bytes=get_input_stride_alignment_bytes(),
     )
     amax8_varlen(logits, seq_lens, out=keys)
     blocks = torch.empty(rows, topk_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=logits.device)

@@ -11,12 +11,189 @@
     load_jit,
     make_cpp_args,
 )
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.utils import is_xpu
 
 from .candidate_table import CANDIDATE_BLOCK_SIZE
 from .utils import make_name
 
 
+def deterministic_topk() -> bool:
+    """Whether a selection must come out the same, in the same order, on every
+    run (SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK). The fused kernels below emit
+    in thread-arrival order, and bf16 ties make even their selected set vary;
+    sparse attention sums in index order, so either changes its output."""
+    return envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK.get()
+
+
+def _deep_select_takes(
+    scores: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    page_table: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    page_size: int = 1,
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether DeepSelect accepts these operands (its single-CTA kernel picks
+    the same set in the same order on every run)."""
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import deep_select
+
+    if not (scores.is_cuda and deep_select.is_deep_select_supported()):
+        return False
+    if scores.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) or out.dtype != torch.int32:
+        return False
+    in_align = deep_select.get_input_stride_alignment_bytes()
+    out_align = deep_select.get_output_stride_alignment_bytes()
+    if scores.dim() != 2 or scores.stride(1) != 1 or scores.data_ptr() % in_align:
+        return False
+    rows, width = scores.shape
+    item = scores.element_size()
+    if not 0 < out.shape[1] <= 4096 or width >= 1 << 23:
+        return False
+    if rows > 1 and scores.stride(0) * item % in_align:
+        return False
+    # DeepSelect reads the last row in whole 128-byte lines.
+    storage = scores.untyped_storage().nbytes() - scores.storage_offset() * item
+    if (
+        rows
+        and (rows - 1) * scores.stride(0) * item + -(-width * item // 128) * 128
+        > storage
+    ):
+        return False
+    if out.dim() != 2 or out.stride(1) != 1 or out.data_ptr() % out_align:
+        return False
+    if (
+        out.shape[1] * 4 % out_align
+        or out.shape[0] > 1
+        and out.stride(0) * 4 % out_align
+    ):
+        return False
+    if page_table is not None:
+        if (
+            page_size <= 0
+            or page_size & (page_size - 1)
+            or page_table.dtype != torch.int32
+        ):
+            return False
+        if page_table.dim() != 2 or page_table.shape[0] != rows:
+            return False
+        pages = page_table.shape[1]
+        if page_table.stride(1) != 1 or pages == 0 or pages * page_size < width:
+            return False
+    return out.shape[0] == rows
+
+
+def _select_positions_torch(
+    scores: torch.Tensor,
+    lens: torch.Tensor,
+    topk: int,
+    starts: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Positions within ``scores[b, starts[b] : starts[b] + lens[b]]`` (``starts``
+    0 when omitted) of the ``topk`` largest scores, ascending, ``-1`` past
+    ``min(topk, lens[b])``. Scores equal to the k-th value go to the lowest
+    positions, so the result never depends on scheduling."""
+    rows, width = scores.shape
+    out = torch.full((rows, topk), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=scores.device)
+    if rows == 0 or width == 0:
+        return out
+    cols = torch.arange(width, dtype=torch.int32, device=scores.device)
+    lo = (
+        torch.zeros((rows, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device=scores.device)
+        if starts is None
+        else starts.reshape(-1, 1).to(torch.int32)
+    )
+    inside = (cols >= lo) & (cols < lo + lens.reshape(-1, 1).to(torch.int32))
+    # Any in-window score, -inf included, must beat the window's outside.
+    s = torch.where(inside, scores.float().clamp(min=-3.0e38), -torch.inf)
+    k = min(topk, width)
+    kth = s.topk(k, dim=-1, sorted=True).values[:, -1:]
+    above = s > kth
+    tie = (s == kth) & inside
+    need = k - above.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True, dtype=torch.int32)
+    take = (above | (tie & (tie.cumsum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.int32) <= need))) & inside
+    key = torch.where(take, cols, width)
+    picked = key.topk(k, dim=-1, largest=False, sorted=True).values
+    out[:, :k] = torch.where(picked < width, picked - lo, -1)
+    return out
+
+
+def _page_transform(
+    positions: torch.Tensor, page_table: torch.Tensor, page_size: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``page_table[b, i // page_size] * page_size + i % page_size``, ``-1`` kept."""
+    valid = positions >= 0
+    i = positions.clamp_min(0).long()
+    slots = page_table.gather(1, i // page_size).long() * page_size + i % page_size
+    return torch.where(valid, slots, -1).to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _deterministic_paged(

+    if out_raw_indices is None and page_table is not None:
+        if _deep_select_takes(scores, out_page_indices, page_table, page_size):

+                scores,
+                topk,
+                page_table=page_table,
+                page_size=page_size,
+                end=lens,
+                output_idx=out_page_indices,
+            )
+            return
+    raw = out_raw_indices if page_table is None else None
+    target = out_page_indices if page_table is None else out_raw_indices
+    if target is not None and _deep_select_takes(scores, target):
+        deep_select.topk(
+            scores, topk, end=lens, output_idx=target, idx_oob_fill_value=-1
+        )
+        positions = target
+    else:
+        positions = _select_positions_torch(scores, lens, topk)

+
+
+def _deterministic_ragged(
+    scores: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    out_offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    out_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    row_starts: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+) -> None:

+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import deep_select
+
+    topk = out_indices.shape[1]
+    lens = seq_lens.reshape(-1).to(torch.int32)
+    if row_starts is None and _deep_select_takes(scores, out_indices):
+        deep_select.topk(
+            scores,
+            topk,
+            end=lens,
+            output_idx=out_indices,
+            output_idx_offset=out_offsets.reshape(-1).to(torch.int32),
+            idx_oob_fill_value=-1,
+        )
+        return
+    positions = _select_positions_torch(scores, lens, topk, row_starts)
+    shifted = positions + out_offsets.reshape(-1, 1).to(torch.int32)
+    out_indices.copy_(torch.where(positions >= 0, shifted, -1))

+"""SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK: the DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 sparse top-k entry
+points pick the same indices in the same order on every run.
+
+The default kernels emit in thread-arrival order (top-k v1/v2, the bf16 candidate
+consumer, DeepSelect's cluster tier), and on tied scores some of them also change
+which positions they keep. Sparse attention sums in index order, so either changes
+greedy outputs between identical requests (#46798). With the flag on, every entry
+point here must return bitwise-identical outputs across eager runs and CUDA-graph
+replays, keep the true top-k scores (as a multiset), and keep the default kernels'
+output contract (page transform, offsets, ``-1`` padding). Each case runs on
+DeepSelect and on the torch selection used when DeepSelect cannot take the operands.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention import deep_select
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import candidate_blocks
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import topk as topk_mod
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not deep_select.is_deep_select_supported(),
+    reason="requires CUDA SM90, SM100, or SM103",
+)
+
+K = 512
+PAGE = 64
+RUNS = 8
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def deterministic_topk():
+    with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_SPARSE_TOPK.override(True):
+        yield
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(params=["deep_select", "torch"])
+def backend(request, monkeypatch):
+    if request.param == "torch":
+        monkeypatch.setattr(topk_mod, "_deep_select_takes", lambda *a, **k: False)
+    return request.param
+
+
+def make_scores(bs: int, n: int, kind: str, seed: int, width: int | None = None):
+    """``kind``: "plateau" keeps fewer than K positive scores and the rest exactly 0
+    (the default v2 kernel then changes its selected set from run to run); "bf16"
+    rounds to bf16 values, which ties the k-th score with dozens of others."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    width = width or (n + 255) // 256 * 256
+    s = torch.randn(bs, width, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    if kind == "plateau":
+        keep = torch.rand(bs, width, generator=g, device="cuda") < 300 / n
+        s = torch.where(keep, s.abs() + 0.01, torch.zeros_like(s))
+    else:
+        s = s.bfloat16().float()
+    lens = torch.full((bs,), n, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    lens[0] = max(1, n // 3)  # a short row: -1 padding when below K
+    pages = -(-width // PAGE)
+    table = torch.stack(
+        [
+            torch.randperm(4 * pages, generator=g, device="cuda")[:pages]
+            for _ in range(bs)
+        ]
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    return s, lens, table
+
+
+def repeat(fn):
+    """RUNS eager outputs, then RUNS replays of one captured graph."""
+    fn()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    outs = [fn().clone() for _ in range(RUNS)]
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        fn()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        out = fn()
+    for _ in range(RUNS):
+        graph.replay()
+        outs.append(out.clone())
+    return outs
+
+
+def check(outs, scores, lens, k, to_positions):
+    first = outs[0]
+    for o in outs[1:]:
+        assert torch.equal(o, first), "output changes between runs"
+    for b in range(scores.shape[0]):
+        n = min(k, int(lens[b]))
+        pos = to_positions(b, first[b].cpu())
+        valid = pos[:n]
+        assert bool((valid >= 0).all()) and bool((pos[n:] == -1).all())
+        assert len(set(valid.tolist())) == n, "an index repeats"
+        assert bool((valid < int(lens[b])).all()), "an index is past the row length"
+        row = scores[b, : int(lens[b])].float()
+        want = row.topk(n).values.sort().values
+        got = scores[b, valid.cuda().long()].float().sort().values
+        assert torch.equal(got, want), "a top-k score is missing"
+
+
+def inverse_page(table_row):
+    inv = {phys: p for p, phys in enumerate(table_row.tolist())}
+
+    def to_pos(slots):
+        return torch.tensor(
+            [inv[v // PAGE] * PAGE + v % PAGE if v >= 0 else -1 for v in slots.tolist()]
+        )
+
+    return to_pos
+
+
+SHAPES = [(1, 300), (1, 8193), (8, 4097), (2, 40000)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["plateau", "bf16"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bs,n", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("entry", ["paged_v2", "raw_v2", "paged_v1"])
+def test_paged(entry, bs, n, kind, backend):
+    s, lens, table = make_scores(bs, n, kind, seed=n + bs)
+    plan = topk_mod.plan_topk_v2(lens)
+
+    def run():
+        out = torch.empty(bs, K, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        if entry == "paged_v2":
+            topk_mod.topk_transform_paged_v2(s, lens, table, out, PAGE, plan)
+        elif entry == "raw_v2":
+            topk_mod.topk_transform_paged_v2(s, lens, None, out, 1, plan)
+        else:
+            topk_mod.topk_transform_paged(s, lens, table, out, PAGE)
+        return out
+
+    if entry == "raw_v2":
+        to_pos = lambda b, row: row  # noqa: E731
+    else:
+        inverses = [inverse_page(table[b].cpu()) for b in range(bs)]
+        to_pos = lambda b, row: inverses[b](row)  # noqa: E731
+    check(repeat(run), s, lens, K, to_pos)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["plateau", "bf16"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bs,n", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_starts", [False, True])
+def test_ragged_v2(bs, n, kind, with_starts, backend):
+    s, lens, _ = make_scores(bs, n, kind, seed=n + bs)
+    offsets = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") * 100000
+    starts = None
+    src = s
+    if with_starts:  # the reference sees each row from its start
+        starts = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") * 7
+        src = torch.full_like(s, -torch.inf)
+        for b in range(bs):
+            st = int(starts[b])
+            src[b, : s.shape[1] - st] = s[b, st:]
+
+    def run():
+        out = torch.empty(bs, K, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        topk_mod.topk_transform_ragged_v2(
+            s, lens, out_offsets=offsets, out_indices=out, row_starts=starts
+        )
+        return out
+
+    to_pos = lambda b, row: torch.where(row >= 0, row - b * 100000, -1)  # noqa: E731
+    check(repeat(run), src, lens, K, to_pos)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["plateau", "bf16"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bs,n", [(1, 8193), (8, 4097), (2, 16384)])
+def test_sparse_consumer(bs, n, kind, backend):
+    """``topk_transform_sparse`` (V4.1 candidate consumers on SM100) over bf16 logits."""
+    s, lens, table = make_scores(bs, n, kind, seed=n + bs)
+    width = (n + 63) // 64 * 64
+    logits = torch.zeros(bs, 2048 * 8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    logits[:, :width] = s[:, :width].bfloat16()
+    sub = torch.arange(8, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    blocks = (table[:, :, None] * 8 + sub).flatten(1)[:, :2048]
+    pad = torch.full(
+        (bs, 2048 - blocks.shape[1]), 2**31 - 1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    blocks = torch.cat([blocks, pad], 1).contiguous()
+
+    def run():
+        out = torch.empty(bs, K, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        topk_mod.topk_transform_sparse(logits, lens, blocks, out)
+        return out
+
+    inverses = [{v: i for i, v in enumerate(blocks[b].tolist())} for b in range(bs)]
+
+    def to_pos(b, row):
+        return torch.tensor(
+            [inverses[b][v // 8] * 8 + v % 8 if v >= 0 else -1 for v in row.tolist()]
+        )
+
+    check(repeat(run), logits, lens, K, to_pos)
+
+
+def test_deep_select_skips_clusters():
+    """bf16 rows past the cluster threshold stay on the single-CTA kernel."""
+    s, lens, table = make_scores(2, 65536, "bf16", seed=7)
+    sb = s.bfloat16()
+
+    def run():
+        out = torch.empty(2, K, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        deep_select.topk_page_transform(
+            sb, K, page_table=table, page_size=PAGE, end=lens, output_idx=out
+        )
+        return out
+
+    inverses = [inverse_page(table[b].cpu()) for b in range(2)]
+    check(repeat(run), sb, lens, K, lambda b, row: inverses[b](row))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bs,width", [(1, 1048580), (3, 20000), (1, 32768)])
+def test_amax_topk_blocks(bs, width, backend):
+    """The V4.1 candidate source's block selection. 1048580 is the ratio-1 score
+    width under a 1M-token context; its block keys are not a multiple of 32 floats."""
+    # rows padded to 128 bytes, as fp4_index_logits_paged allocates them
+    padded, lens, _ = make_scores(
+        bs, min(width, 40000), "bf16", seed=bs, width=-(-width // 32) * 32
+    )
+    s = padded[:, :width]
+    nblocks = (lens + 7) // 8
+    cols = torch.arange(padded.shape[1], device="cuda")
+    keys = padded.masked_fill(cols >= lens[:, None], -torch.inf)
+    keys = keys.view(bs, -1, 8).amax(-1)
+    keys[torch.arange(bs, device="cuda"), nblocks.long() - 1] = torch.inf
+
+    def run():
+        return candidate_blocks.amax_topk_blocks(s, lens, nblocks, 2048)
+
+    check(repeat(run), keys, nblocks, 2048, lambda b, row: row)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
